name: Sauna belt

card.summary: A heated or heat-retaining waist wrap that sellers market for sweating, slimming the midsection and reducing the look of cellulite.
card.aka: Sweat belt, hot body shaper, heating belt
card.note: Case reports link heated abdominal belts to a heat-induced skin discoloration (erythema ab igne); overheating and dehydration are other noted risks.

quick.overview:
Sauna belts are waist wraps, either electrically heated or made from neoprene or rubber that traps heat, worn to make the midsection sweat. People use them hoping for a slimmer-looking waist and smoother abdominal skin.

Sellers say heating the abdomen burns more fat. Critics and clinicians quoted in consumer coverage say water loss returns on rehydration, and the Mayo Clinic's Edward Laskowski has said girdles only temporarily compress fat and skin.
quick.how: Products are advertised for wear during exercise or chores, often for a couple of hours at a time. Electrically heated versions exist as well; a Korean utility-model patent from 2006 describes a sauna belt using electrical heating.
quick.risks: A 2009 case report in the International Journal of Dermatology described erythema ab igne, a net-like heat-induced skin discoloration, after sauna belt use for abdominal obesity and cellulite. Commentators also list dehydration, overheating and restricted breathing, and say heat-related weight loss is mostly water.

lead: A sauna belt is a waist wrap that heats or holds heat against the abdomen, marketed for sweating and for a slimmer, smoother midsection. [1][2]
Sellers say the heat helps burn abdominal fat; commentators in consumer media argue the weight lost is mostly water that returns on rehydration. [3]
A 2009 dermatology case report described erythema ab igne following sauna belt use for abdominal obesity and cellulite. [1]

chain: Belt traps or generates heat at the waist
Temporarily slimmer-looking waist (as claimed for fat loss)
angle.text: Sellers present the belt as a way to slim the waist and tone the abdomen. Compression and water loss can change the midsection's look temporarily, according to commentators.

infobox: Rubber, neoprene or other non-breathable fabrics; electric versions exist

paras: Sauna belts, also called sweat belts or hot body shapers, are corset-like garments made of rubber, neoprene or other non-breathable materials, in a line of shapewear that includes corsets and waist trainers. [3] A Korean utility-model patent from 2006 describes a sauna belt using electrical heating. [2]
Sellers say heating the abdomen burns more fat, especially during exercise, and that belts slim and tone. Products are advertised for gym or home workouts and chores, often for a couple of hours. [3]

Gary Hunter of the University of Alabama at Birmingham told the LA Times that the belly is a major site of heat loss, so belts could be dangerous. Edward Laskowski of the Mayo Clinic wrote that girdles temporarily compress and redistribute fat and skin. [3] The American Board of Cosmetic Surgery, as cited by the same article, says waist trainers can reduce lung capacity. [3]

A 2009 case report described erythema ab igne after sauna belt use for abdominal obesity and cellulite. [1] Erythema ab igne is a net-like redness or darkening caused by repeated infrared heat; stopping the heat source is the first treatment, and rare skin cancers have been reported after decades of exposure. [4][5] Consumer coverage also lists dehydration, heat stroke and restricted breathing. [3]

No controlled studies of sauna belts for fat loss were found. The 2009 International Journal of Dermatology report on erythema ab igne following sauna belt use is a case report. [1] A small 2010 study of corsets, cited in consumer coverage, could not draw conclusions because most participants stopped wearing them. [3]
